problem: Portal V2 had a canonical experience layer, but release assurance still sampled only three routes and three viewports and did not fail on dynamic visual overflow, missing experience runtime or undersized critical interaction targets.
rootCause: The visual regression harness measured legacy oversized components but was not yet bound to the full cross-cutting experience runtime and therefore could miss regressions in dynamically mounted views and narrow-mobile interactions.
root_cause: The visual regression harness measured legacy oversized components but was not yet bound to the full cross-cutting experience runtime and therefore could miss regressions in dynamically mounted views and narrow-mobile interactions.
prevention: Keep portal-v2/experience.css and portal-v2/experience.js as the single final experience authority.
Normalize and remeasure dynamically mounted visuals with MutationObserver and ResizeObserver.
Fail visual assurance on page overflow above 2px, marked visual overflow, missing v2 runtime or critical controls below 44px.
Exercise six critical routes at 1440px, 1024px, 390px and 320px, producing 24 screenshots per assurance run.
Do not widen thresholds to conceal structural responsive defects.
Keep canonical Portal State auth and fail-closed write confirmation unchanged.

evidence.outcome: Visual assurance is release-blocking and emits screenshot plus metric evidence for the 24 route/viewport combinations.
